pieces.text: Coral reefs help humans in many ways. The ways in which an ecosystem benefits humans are called
. Here are a few examples of the ecosystem services provided by coral reefs.

mainText.text: Every year, humans eat millions of tons of fish, shellfish, and other seafood. Many of the species we eat need coral reefs in order to survive and reproduce.
Corals can shield beaches and islands from waves. This reduces erosion that could wash away sand or damage buildings. A coral reef can also protect against storms and floods near the ocean.

Coral reefs are part of the histories and traditions of people around the world. For example, the Aboriginal people of Australia have fished on coral reefs for thousands of years. They have traditional legends, songs, and art about the reefs and their animals.

contents.text: Ecosystem services are ways in which an ecosystem benefits humans.

explanationText.text: Cultural value is a benefit for humans that an ecosystem can provide. For example, coral reefs and their animals are important to the Aboriginal culture in Australia.

Flooding in towns may occur in some ecosystems. However, flooding in towns often hurts humans and damages property. Because flooding in towns usually does not benefit humans, it is unlikely to be an ecosystem service.
Food is a benefit for humans that an ecosystem can provide. For example, coral reefs provide seafood for humans around the world.

Protection from predators is a benefit that an ecosystem can provide for prey in the ecosystem. However, humans are unlikely to be prey. Because protection from predators usually does not benefit humans, it is unlikely to be an ecosystem service.

contents.text: Ecosystem services are ways in which an ecosystem benefits humans.

explanationText.text: Protection from predators is a benefit that an ecosystem can provide for prey in the ecosystem. However, humans are unlikely to be prey. Because protection from predators usually does not benefit humans, it is unlikely to be an ecosystem service.
Food is a benefit for humans that an ecosystem can provide. For example, coral reefs provide seafood for humans around the world.

Flooding in towns may occur in some ecosystems. However, flooding in towns often hurts humans and damages property. Because flooding in towns usually does not benefit humans, it is unlikely to be an ecosystem service.
Cultural value is a benefit for humans that an ecosystem can provide. For example, coral reefs and their animals are important to the Aboriginal culture in Australia.
